themeScoping.name: default-world
themeScoping.purpose: Default token values. Still governs every /admin route and every component rendered outside the customer-facing branch.

themeScoping.name: storefront-world
themeScoping.value: html:has(.storefront-shell) { color-scheme: dark; } — dark olive + gold
themeScoping.purpose: The homepage studio hero's world promoted to the whole customer-facing palette. Re-points the same token names, so every component flips colour without a markup change. Sets color-scheme: dark and the root scrollbar pairing (cocoa-300 on paper, thin).

themeScoping.name: scoping-class
themeScoping.purpose: isAdminRoute is true only for /admin and /admin/*, and the admin arm renders a wrapper with no storefront-shell class, so admin never matches the :has() selector.

themeScoping.name: theme-block-mode
themeScoping.purpose: Load-bearing. Without inline, generated utilities reference their token by name (bg-parchment compiles to var(--color-parchment)), so the storefront block can re-point one set of token names. With inline the hex would be baked into the utility and a second parallel vocabulary would be required.

themeScoping.name: dark-scope-overrides
themeScoping.purpose: Only the values a var() cannot re-point: the gold-on-ink primary action, the color-mix outline ground, badge label colour, the selection pair, and brightness lifts for the raster logo and wax seal. Focus, eyebrow, ghost and chip-active need no override because honey-600/700 re-point on their own.

themeScoping.name: photo-mat
themeScoping.value: bg-sand-100, identical in both themes, not re-pointed
themeScoping.purpose: The storefront's only light surface. Catalog photography was shot on a warm sand studio ground, so the same plate in both worlds is what makes honey colour comparable. Photographs are mix-blend-multiply into it; a product with no photo gets ProductArt's dark dashed well instead.

shadows.name: warm-sm
shadows.purpose: Shared panels and resting primary buttons. Warm shadows read as depth on paper; on the dark comb they have to be near-black to register at all.

shadows.name: warm
shadows.purpose: Primary-button hover and card hover. The storefront override is applied on .storefront-shell .btn-primary:hover, because the base lift is invisible on the comb.

shadows.name: warm-lg
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, the cart drawer, the mobile nav drawer, select content and the scroll-to-top button.

motion.name: studio-camera
motion.purpose: Native scrolling drives front, side, cap detail, label detail and return camera views; pause holds the current view and reduced motion fixes the opening view. No wheel interception and no scroll replacement.

motion.name: chapter-copy
motion.purpose: Crossfades the five studio copy phases; disabled under reduced motion.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.purpose: Language switch and route changes cross-fade; the shared product-<id> name morphs the card thumbnail into the detail image. Snapshots keep their default fade so an unmatched outgoing image does not freeze.

motion.name: brand-signatures
motion.value: wordmark-sheen 7s ease-in-out infinite; honey-pulse 3.2s; honey-drop-bob 4s; brand-rise 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)
motion.purpose: The brand mark's quiet motion. Continuous animation runs only on the initial full page load: html.has-nav, added in beforeNavigate, disables animate-fade-up and animate-float to avoid a flicker on every client-side navigation.

motion.name: feedback
motion.value: shimmer 1.5s; added-check 0.3s ease forwards; pop-in 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); spin 0.6s linear infinite; fade-up 0.7s
motion.purpose: Skeletons, cart confirmation, badge pop, spinner and section entrance.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce collapses every animation, transition and scroll-behavior to 0.01ms / auto
motion.purpose: Global kill switch. The hero also collapses its 360svh scroll area into a static introduction of the same viewport height and hides the viewpoint buttons, scroll prompt and motion toggle.

breakpoints.name: home-grid-break
breakpoints.value: 900px (6-column category grid to 3), 600px (product grid to 2, category grid to 2)

breakpoints.name: nav-break
breakpoints.value: 1024px (desktop nav and search swap to the mobile drawer; the drawer auto-closes above it)

narrative.northStar: A dark comb: deep olive ground, honey-gold for every action, ivory type, and real catalog photography on warm sand plates
narrative.overview: The system has two color worlds on one token set. The light paper palette declared in the @theme block on :root is the default and still governs every /admin route. The homepage studio hero's dark olive and gold world was promoted from a homepage-local treatment to the whole customer-facing palette; it is declared in html:has(.storefront-shell), which re-points the same token names so every component flips colour without a markup change. cocoa-50 becomes the storefront's darkest ground and cocoa-900 becomes ivory body text. src/routes/+layout.svelte applies storefront-shell on the customer-facing branch only, so admin never matches the :has() selector. The @theme block is deliberately not inline: utilities must resolve through var() so one set of token names can serve both scopes. The sand photography family is the storefront's only light surface and is identical in both themes, so a product photo always sits on the same plate and honey colour reads true. Physical depth stays in the studio scene: lathed glass, a dark honey volume, a ridged white cap, a soft shadow floor and a transparent 0x141611 clear colour behind the page.
keyCharacteristics: One token vocabulary, two scoped values per token, one sand family that never changes.
Dark olive ground with raised olive steps and 1px cocoa borders; ivory body text whose muted steps are tinted in the same yellow-green family, never neutral gray.
Honey-600 carries every primary action, active state, focus ring, underline and skip link; gold on ink-950.
Catalog photography is multiplied into a warm sand plate; a product with no photo gets a dark dashed well instead.
Rounded glass, a dark honey volume and a white ridged cap under studio lighting, lit from within by a pinned hero stage.
Readable bilingual typography with Arabic RTL and English LTR from the same components.
44px storefront controls, visible focus, native scrolling and a global reduced-motion kill switch.
rules: Build surfaces from the existing token names (bg-parchment, text-cocoa-900, border-cocoa-200, text-honey-600) so they resolve in both worlds without a new rule.
Add a .storefront-shell-prefixed override only for a value a var() cannot re-point, and record it in DESIGN.md.
Put catalog photography on .photo-mat and multiply it in; it is the single place to change if the client later wants photographs blended into the ground.
Keep the light paper palette on /admin. It is a deliberate second world, not a leftover.
dos: Do preserve the existing name, logo, product photos and Arabic RTL / English LTR behavior.
Do build new surfaces from the existing token names so they resolve correctly in both worlds without a new rule.
Do keep the dark olive and honey-gold world as the storefront's palette everywhere a customer can see it, including the header, catalog, cart, checkout and account.
Do keep the light paper palette on /admin; it is a deliberate second world, not a leftover.
Do put catalog photography on .photo-mat and multiply it in.
Do give a product with no photo the dark dashed well (ProductArt), never an empty bright plate.
Do keep shopping links and product information usable before the scene loads.
Do use reduced-motion behavior, visible focus and 44px storefront controls.
Do keep @theme non-inline. Inlining the values breaks per-scope re-pointing.
Do add a .storefront-shell-prefixed override only for values a var() cannot express, and record it.
donts: Don't reintroduce the rejected playful dipper, droplets or separate animated story treatment.
Don't present the procedural jar as a scan or exact packaging photograph.
Don't require an animation to finish before shopping or replace native scrolling.
Don't put a hard-coded hex in a component that should re-point with the theme.
Don't use sand for anything other than photographic plates, or use mix-blend-multiply outside the photographic surfaces already listed.
Don't invent product benefits, testimonials, certifications or delivery promises.
